source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

ABB.report_year: CY2023 (ABB India Annual Report 2023, most recent available)

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A 'Business environment' section: supply chain resilience, onshoring and friend-shoring trends create opportunities for India to attract manufacturing and alternative value chains; manufacturing opportunity for India is growing because MNCs are picking India as a manufacturing and export hub to diversify their supply base to reduce geopolitical and economic risks. MD&A also states ABB India continued its journey of 'Making in India for India and the world.' Motion segment exports surged ~28% in 2023. China is not named explicitly; framing is industry/India-level rather than company-specific China+1.

govt_capex.evidence: No explicit % of revenue disclosed, but strong qualitative linkage: MD&A cites resurgence in capital expenditure driven by government infrastructure expansion. Major orders during the year include GIS for a major rail bridge, traction switchgear for a flagship semi-high-speed rail project, Motion traction solutions for metro systems and Indian Railways, and equipment orders under a state government's healthcare initiative. Outlook cites government investments in power transmission, railways, metro, and public infrastructure as a growth driver.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Key Financial Ratios note: Interest Coverage Ratio and Debt Equity Ratio marked Not Applicable, as the Company did not have any borrowings in the current and previous year. Debt-Equity ratio of 0.01x is driven only by lease liabilities, not bank borrowings. Company held a net cash balance and funded capex from internal accruals.

crude_exposure.evidence: No explicit crude-oil-linked raw material % disclosed. Financial risk management note discloses commodity price risk hedging via commodity future contracts for Copper and Silver used in switchgear/motor/electrical components manufacturing. No mention of plastics/polymer or direct crude-oil linkage.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company conservatively hedges foreign currency exposure at the point of commitment or at balance sheet date to protect contract margins, using foreign exchange forward and option contracts; no speculative derivative trading is permitted.
inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue by geography: Within India ₹9,357.81 crore, Outside India ₹1,088.71 crore, Total ₹10,446.52 crore (CY2023), i.e. exports ~10.4% of revenue. Forex risk arises primarily with respect to CHF, USD, SEK and EUR. Exports/imports are largely intercompany with ABB Group fellow subsidiaries. Company held net cash of ~₹4,727 crore including treasury bills.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI is referenced only as a sector-level growth driver/opportunity in the MD&A Outlook (focus on local manufacturing with PLI scheme, expansion of railways and metros), not as a confirmed direct benefit to ABB India. No statement that ABB India itself has been approved for or receives PLI incentives/revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: No Alkem-specific China+1 diversification narrative found. Alkem sources some APIs (e.g., potassium clavulanate) from India's Bulk Drug PLI-scheme beneficiary companies (e.g., Kinvan) rather than running its own China-diversification program.

rural.evidence: Alkem has historically strong distribution in rural markets, using in-house field agents; leveraged acute-therapy dominance to grow trade generics, a distributor-led business that gained traction in Tier 2/3 towns since COVID-19. No specific rural/tier-town revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Per secondary reporting of CFO/earnings-call commentary, approximately 80% of forex exposure is reported hedged (not independently verified against primary AR text).
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 international sales were ~29.8% of total revenue (India sales Rs 8,983.7 cr, international Rs 3,821 cr); within international, US business alone contributed approximately 22% of total FY25 revenue, with Rest-of-World markets accounting for ~7.8%.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence Alkem itself is a direct PLI beneficiary; sources some APIs from PLI-scheme beneficiary suppliers (e.g., Kinvan) rather than being a PLI awardee itself.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bharat Forge is described as adding manufacturing/engineering capacity in the US and Europe to serve OEMs locally and capture share amid China+1 supply-chain shifts; positioned among top Indian auto-component/forging exporters seen as beneficiaries of Western OEMs diversifying away from China. Could not confirm exact wording in FY25 MD&A since AR PDF was inaccessible.

rural.evidence: Domestic Agriculture/Tractor-linked segment described as recovering in FY25 driven by strong growth in rural India; no explicit % of total revenue tied to rural/agri disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 consolidated defence revenue ~Rs 1,700 crore (Kalyani Strategic Systems ~Rs 1,567 crore, largely exports) against consolidated FY25 revenue of Rs 15,123 crore, implying ~11% (derived, not company-stated). Standalone defence order book cited as ~70% of standalone revenue base (order book, not realized revenue). Domestic CV/infra-linked segment also cited as helped by government infrastructure/capex spending pickup in H2 FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Older (pre-FY24) notes indicate Bharat Forge borrows largely in foreign currency at floating rates (LIBOR/EURIBOR-linked) with natural hedge from exports; no FY24-25-specific floating-rate % confirmed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Qualitative only: company described as relying on natural hedging (foreign-currency debt offset by foreign-currency/export earnings); no explicit hedging policy text confirmed from primary source.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~30% of consolidated FY25 revenue; company is India's largest exporter of auto/forged components with US/Europe as key markets.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bharat Forge is listed among companies approved under the 'Component Champion' category of the Auto PLI scheme for Advanced Automotive Technology products, alongside Sona BLW, Bosch, Delphi-TVS. No revenue/benefit percentage disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Trade press (Autocar Professional, 2025) on Bosch's India operations: India is emerging as a major export hub for Bosch, with 10-11% of the company's exports from India currently focused on hydraulic components, with efforts underway to expand this share, particularly in electrification. By localizing production of power electronics and controller units, Bosch is positioning India as a vital node in its global supply chain. No AR text was directly readable to confirm explicit company-authored China+1 framing.

rural.evidence: FY2024-25 results (Bosch Media Service India): Mobility business sector reported a 7.0% increase in product sales, largely driven by growth in overall passenger and tractor segments; Powertrain Solutions division saw a 5.8% increase driven by growth in the tractor segment and an increase in export sales. Indicates rural/tractor demand is a cited growth driver, but no revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party reporting notes India-sourced hydraulic-component exports (~10-11% of Bosch's exports from India) ship globally including to North America, implying meaningful USD-linked export exposure, but no percentage or hedging-policy disclosure was confirmed from primary filings.

pli_scheme.evidence: Per India Briefing and Ministry of Heavy Industries PLI-Auto scheme coverage, Bosch Limited is listed among approved Component Champion beneficiaries under India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components Industry (approved March 2022). No revenue % or incentive amount specific to Bosch disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: D-Mart (Avenue Supermarts) is a pure domestic brick-and-mortar/online retail chain sourcing FMCG, grocery, apparel and general merchandise largely from Indian suppliers/manufacturers for sale in India. No China+1, supply-chain diversification, or manufacturing-relocation narrative was found.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural/semi-urban revenue percentage disclosed. Secondary sources indicate DMart's cluster-based expansion strategy is pushing into underpenetrated North and East India and Tier-2/Tier-3 cities, while ~75% of existing stores remain concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. FY25 saw 50 new stores added (415 stores across 10 states), but no tier-wise or rural/urban revenue split was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: D-Mart has historically operated an almost debt-free balance sheet (near-zero net debt, EBIT covering interest ~282x per Simply Wall St). No explicit floating-vs-fixed borrowing rate split disclosed; given near-debt-free status, floating-rate interest exposure appears minimal.

inr_exposure.evidence: No export or USD-denominated revenue found. D-Mart's business (including DMart Ready e-commerce) is entirely India-focused with no foreign segment or export revenue reported.

IKS Health is a technology-enabled healthcare solutions provider serving US, Canada and Australia physician enterprises from India-based delivery centers, with over 90% of revenue from repeat US clients; FY25 revenue rose 47% YoY to Rs 2,664 crore. This implies the large majority of revenue is USD-denominated, but no exact geography % breakdown, USD revenue %, or hedging policy disclosure was accessible.

rural.evidence: No rural revenue % disclosed. IHCL's Ginger brand (100+ hotels as of FY25) is expanding into Tier 2/Tier 3 cities alongside state capitals and gateway cities; no revenue split by city tier found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL (standalone) reported net debt as nil as of FY2024-25, with finance costs of Rs 208.38 crore (down YoY), indicating very low overall debt levels. Exact floating vs fixed rate split for outstanding borrowings not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Standalone foreign exchange earnings were Rs 733.28 crore in FY2024-25 against forex outgo of Rs 81.65 crore. Consolidated revenue ~Rs 8,565 crore; enterprise/system-wide revenue Rs 14,836 crore reflecting a meaningful international hotel portfolio, but no clean domestic vs international revenue % breakdown found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable to the hospitality sector.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company widely reported as 'almost debt free'; no detailed floating vs fixed rate borrowing breakdown found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/CDMO/API exports were ~42% of FY25 consolidated revenue (Domestic Rs2,269cr, International Rs1,128cr, CDMO Rs446cr, API Rs76cr), including US (via Rising Pharma, cost-plus model), Russia/CIS, and South Africa; exact USD-denominated % and hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of PLI scheme participation found; JB Chemicals' business is formulations/CDMO-weighted rather than bulk-drug/API PLI-scale manufacturing.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's integrated report/business review materials discuss multi-sourcing strategies, long-term vendor contracts, and local backward integration into key APIs to manage input volatility, and note that 'China Plus One sourcing diversification by global pharma companies is creating strong and durable demand for Indian API manufacturers' -- positioning Lupin's India-based manufacturing and CDMO operations favorably amid US-China trade tensions. Found via search snippets of Lupin's Integrated Report 2024-25, not a verbatim AR quote confirmed by direct PDF read.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin uses cash flow hedges (forward contracts/derivatives) for forecasted foreign currency transactions per its accounting policy notes.
inr_exposure.evidence: US sales were USD 925 Mn in FY2025 (up from USD 815 Mn in FY2024), representing about 36% of Lupin's global sales per the company's FY2025 results press release; detailed hedge notional/coverage % not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is cited among major Indian pharma companies (alongside Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's, Cipla, Aurobindo) that have leveraged India's PLI scheme for Key Starting Materials/Drug Intermediates/APIs (outlay ~Rs 15,000 crore, FY21-FY29) to invest in domestic API/backward-integration manufacturing capacity; specific incentive amount or revenue % attributable to Lupin not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company markets in-house API manufacturing at USFDA/WHO-GMP approved facilities in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh (~500 MT installed capacity), supplying APIs to 100+ countries, and describes backward integration reducing external dependencies. Trade press reports Mankind completed a multi-year overhaul of its global supply chain and strategic procurement operations, but no explicit China+1 framing found.

rural.evidence: Per third-party summaries of the Mankind Pharma FY25 annual report, domestic sales by city class were: Metro 23%, Town Class 1 27%, Town Class 2-6 28%, Rural 22% (i.e. Tier2-6 + Rural ~50% of domestic sales). Company historically over-indexed vs IPM average on Class II-IV + rural sales mix.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is reported to be in a large net-cash position (~Rs 3,138 crore free cash and bank balances plus Rs 931 crore liquid investments as of Dec-2024 per ICRA rating rationale), suggesting limited reliance on floating-rate debt, but the specific breakdown could not be retrieved.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (largely USD/foreign-currency denominated) was approximately Rs 1,532 crore of Rs 12,207 crore total FY25 revenue (~12.5%), up from ~7.8% in FY24, indicating a rapidly growing but still modest USD/export revenue exposure. No specific forex hedging policy language could be retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI schemes for Bulk Drugs/APIs and Pharmaceuticals had 55 approved applicants; first tranche of incentive releases named Dr. Reddy's, Biocon, Strides Pharma Science, and Premier Medical Corporation as beneficiaries. No source could confirm Mankind Pharma is an officially approved PLI applicant/beneficiary.

rural.evidence: As of Q2 FY25 (Sep 30 2024), NIMF's AUM from Beyond the Top 30 cities (B-30) stood at Rs 1.32 trillion (USD 14.9 billion), up 15% YoY, forming 19.8% of NIMF's AUM vs. 18.6% for the industry. This is B30-city AUM share, used as the closest proxy for 'rural' exposure for an AMC business; exact FY2024-25 full-year annual-report figure could not be confirmed since the AR PDF was inaccessible.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial analysis describes Nippon Life India AMC as almost debt free; no floating-rate borrowings identified. As an AUM-fee-based asset manager, this signal has limited relevance to the business model.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/brokerage commentary states Navin Fluorine is benefiting from rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment, capturing customers de-risking supply chains away from China; on the input side, NFIL has entered long-term supply contracts with South African miners for fluorspar, partially de-risking sourcing from China. This came from brokerage/analyst summaries, not a confirmed verbatim quote from the AR MD&A itself.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials cited are fluorspar, sulfuric acid, and hydrofluoric acid (HF) feedstocks — not crude-oil-linked. No quantified crude/petrochemical raw-material exposure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution to revenue reported around ~63-65% for FY24/FY25 (with quarterly variation, e.g. 77% in Q4FY25). Specific forex hedging/forward-contract policy text was not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: A dedicated PLI scheme for the specialty chemicals/fluorochemicals sector was reported as being proposed/in the pipeline by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers; no confirmation found that Navin Fluorine is a confirmed beneficiary under an active PLI scheme.

rural.evidence: Company discloses rural/semi-urban 'RUrban' distribution expansion: reach grew from ~110,000 to ~209,000 villages over the last three years, with 28,240 rural distribution points added since the RUrban model launched in 2019. No explicit % of total revenue attributed to rural markets was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Nestle India is described in multiple secondary sources as predominantly a domestic-revenue company with exports forming a small share of sales, but no verified/quoted percentage or hedging policy statement from the Annual Report itself could be retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: A 2020 Business Standard article quoted Nestle India's then-CMD stating the company was 'planning to avail' the government's PLI scheme to boost exports; some undated secondary summaries list Nestle India among PLI food-processing scheme beneficiaries. No confirmation of current beneficiary status found in the AR itself, treated as unconfirmed.

rural.evidence: Nykaa's offline retail footprint expanded from 63 stores in 34 cities (FY2020) to 237 stores in 79 cities (FY2025); nearly half of ~50 new FY25 stores opened in Tier-II/III markets, with growth cited in non-metro cities including Jaipur, Lucknow, Patna, Indore, Guwahati, Surat, Nagpur and Bhopal. No specific Tier 2/3 or rural revenue percentage found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Search snippets indicate Phoenix Mills' average cost of debt fell to ~7.68% in FY25 (long-term debt ~Rs 3,847 cr as of Mar-2025, net debt/equity ~0.24), consistent with rate-linked (floating) borrowings such as lease rental discounting (LRD) loans and bank facilities common to Indian mall/office developers, but no explicit fixed-vs-floating % breakdown from the AR notes to financial statements could be retrieved.

rural.evidence: Radico's strength lies in adapting: launching new-age premium products while continuing to dominate in semi-urban and rural segments with trusted value brands; pan-India sales network reaching over 60,000 retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration.

crude_exposure.evidence: Packaging costs are roughly 25% of sales; cost of grain, ENA (extra neutral alcohol), and glass has been volatile. Company shifting from glass to PET bottles in the regular segment (PET is a petrochemical/crude-linked input). No explicit % of raw material cost tied to crude oil disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export sales contribute approximately 6.56% of total turnover; exports to over 100 countries including North America, Europe, Africa, and Asia.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages are not among the sectors covered under India's PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR discusses broad diversification (geography, product, customer, powertrain) and geopolitical/tariff risk, but never frames growth via explicit 'China+1' reshoring language; the company itself runs a manufacturing plant in China. Sourcing diversification mentioned is tied to Red Sea shipping disruption, not China-specific supply-chain relocation.

rural.evidence: Not applicable — B2B auto-components exporter to global OEMs; no rural/consumer revenue segment disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: No FY2024-25 revenue tied to government capex. Company entered railway equipment business (Escorts Kubota Railway Division acquisition, closed 1 June 2025 = FY25-26) citing India rail infrastructure growth as a forward-looking driver, but not part of FY2024-25 numbers.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated interest-rate-risk note: Variable rate borrowings INR 134.63mn, Fixed rate borrowings INR Nil, Total borrowings INR 134.63mn as at 31-Mar-2025 (100% floating). Company is net-cash (net debt -INR 9,586.93mn).

crude_exposure.evidence: Material cost = 43% of total income (INR 15,447mn), comprising steel alloy bars, iron castings, copper wires, aluminium die castings, bearings, magnets and plastic moulded components — plastics/rubber not separately quantified as a % tied to crude oil derivatives.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy; Company primarily uses forward contracts to hedge USD/EUR currency risk from international sales and overseas purchases.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company operates internationally with a large portion of business transacted in US$ and EUR, using currency hedging based upon a Board approved hedging policy which primarily employs forward contracts. Outstanding forward contracts at 31-Mar-2025: USD 109.55mn and EUR 20.81mn (receivable side). 71% of FY24-25 revenue is export (NA 41%, Europe 24%, Asia 6%, other 0.3%), implying majority FX-denominated revenue, but no exact USD-revenue % disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review states the company benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which it had eight products approved. Board's Report confirms approval for Suspension Motor for electric two-wheelers under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. No revenue/incentive amount or % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Broader Indian pharma/API industry sources describe a China Plus One sourcing trend for KSMs/APIs benefiting Indian bulk-drug manufacturers generally, but no source found where Sun Pharma's own annual report explicitly frames its growth or export orders around China+1/supply-chain diversification.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix reported in Sun Pharma investor materials: India Formulations 33%, US 31%, Emerging Markets 18%, Rest of World (incl. Western Europe and Japan) 14% - implying roughly 60-65% of consolidated revenue is international/export-linked, though a specific consolidated USD revenue % figure and hedging policy text could not be confirmed from directly-read AR sections.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs exists and Sun Pharma is a major player in the injectable generics/API space where the scheme operates, but no source found confirming Sun Pharma specifically as an approved PLI beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: No disclosure found of Titan diversifying gemstone/component sourcing away from China. Titan's FY25 diversification narrative relates to launching its own lab-grown diamond brand 'beYon' for product-mix reasons, not China+1 supply-chain relocation.

rural.evidence: Tanishq (jewellery division) has an active Tier-2/Tier-3 town expansion strategy: plans to enter ~130 new small towns and add ~200 outlets over the next 5 years using smaller-format stores suited to B & C towns. No explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable/disclosed as a crude-oil linkage. Titan's key raw materials are gold, silver and diamonds (jewellery) rather than crude-oil-derived inputs.

inr_exposure.evidence: Titan has a small and growing international jewellery (Tanishq/Mia) footprint - 23 stores as of FY25 across UAE, USA and Singapore. Q4FY25 international jewellery revenue was ~Rs 402 crore versus a full-year Jewellery division total income of ~Rs 46,571 crore, implying international/export revenue is a small single-digit-or-less percentage of jewellery revenue, but an explicit consolidated export % was not obtainable.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention found of Titan being a PLI scheme beneficiary; Titan is primarily a domestic retail/consumer brand (jewellery, watches, eyewear) rather than a manufacturer in PLI-eligible sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent has pursued API backward integration (e.g., acquisition of Glochem API plant, capacity expansion/debottlenecking at Dahej and Indrad) aimed at reducing input cost vulnerability and import dependency for APIs used in ANDA filings; not explicitly framed as 'China+1' in sources reviewed, could not verify against actual AR text.

inr_exposure.evidence: Torrent has multi-currency international revenue (Brazil-BRL, Germany-EUR, US-USD, other EM currencies) implying material foreign-currency exposure, but specific hedging policy and USD-only revenue % could not be retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs targets ~41 critical APIs historically imported from China; Torrent has emphasized API backward integration, but no source confirms Torrent as a named PLI beneficiary.
